The gene therapy landscape has evolved substantially in recent years, beginning with the approval of the first adeno-associated virus-based gene therapy, Luxterna, in 2017. Since then, the US FDA has approved nearly 30 new viral gene therapy programs, with notable examples including Zolgensma, Spinraza, Hemgenix, Zynteglo, Lyfgenia, Kymriah, Skysona, and Tecelra. Remarkably, all these products rely on delivery via adeno-associated vectors (AAVs) and lentiviral vectors (LVs).
